basic_details.scholarship_name: Georgia Tech Graduate Research & Teaching Assistantship (GRA/GTA)
basic_details.host_institutions_covered: Georgia Institute of Technology (Atlanta, Georgia, USA)
basic_details.major_restrictions: Open to doctoral students across all engineering and computing schools: College of Computing (Computer Science, Machine Learning, Cybersecurity), College of Engineering (Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical & Computer Engineering, Biomedical, Civil, Chemical, Industrial & Systems Engineering), and College of Sciences.
basic_details.number_of_awards_total: ~400 to 500 new fully funded doctoral assistantships awarded annually across departments
basic_details.number_of_awards_pakistan: Open global competition; virtually all admitted full-time PhD students receive full tuition waiver and monthly stipend (typically 4 to 10 Pakistani doctoral students admitted/yr)
basic_details.duration_of_scholarship: Full duration of doctoral studies (typically 4 to 5 years, subject to satisfactory research performance)

nationality_requirements: Open to international students of all nationalities holding F-1 or J-1 student visas
eligibility_requirements.academic_qualifications: Completed Bachelor's degree (16 years education) or Master's degree in engineering, computer science, mathematics, or related field with top honors.
eligibility_requirements.grading_conversion_notes: Minimum 3.70+ / 4.00 CGPA; competitive admitted students typically possess 3.85+ CGPA or top 5% class standing.
eligibility_requirements.subject_background_prerequisites: Advanced mathematics, programming, systems, and engineering fundamentals aligned with chosen graduate program.
eligibility_requirements.current_education_status: Graduated or currently in final semester of undergraduate/master's degree.
eligibility_requirements.work_experience_notes: Peer-reviewed research publications, conference presentations, and lab experience heavily prioritized.

english_proficiency.notes: TOEFL iBT min 90 (subscores 19+; College of Computing requires 100+), IELTS Academic min 7.0 (reading 6.5, listening 6.5, speaking 6.5, writing 5.5).

eligibility_requirements.gender_specific_requirements: Equal opportunity; female engineers and computer scientists encouraged.

tuition_fee.details: Full tuition waiver reducing out-of-state tuition ($33,000+/yr) to a nominal student fee of $25 per semester.

admission_application_fee.details: Georgia Tech graduate application fee ($105 for international applicants) paid by applicant.

accommodation.details: Paid out of monthly research stipend; on-campus graduate living (Tenth & Home) or off-campus apartments in Midtown/Home Park Atlanta (~$800–1,200/mo).

monthly_stipend.details: Graduate Research Assistantship (GRA) stipend of ~$2,600 to $3,200/month (~USD $31,200 to $38,400/year / ~PKR 725,000 to 890,000/month).

visa_fee.details: US F-1 Visa application fee ($185) and SEVIS I-901 fee ($350) paid by applicant.

health_insurance.details: Georgia Tech Student Health Insurance Plan (SHIP) subsidized (institution pays ~85-90% of premium).

books_and_materials_allowance.details: Departmental research computing infrastructure, lab equipment, and software provided.

research_funding_conference_grant.details: Research supervisor grants and Georgia Tech SGA Conference Travel Grants cover expenses for presenting at top conferences.

travel_transit_allowance.details: Tech Trolley and campus transit system are free; MARTA public transit pass discounted for students.

university_and_program_options.single_or_multiple_universities: Single institution: Georgia Institute of Technology (Atlanta, GA, USA).
university_and_program_options.university_rankings_scope: #3 globally in Industrial Engineering, Top 5 globally in Mechanical, Aerospace, and Civil Engineering, #6 in Computer Science (US News).
available_majors: Computer Science, Machine Learning, Cybersecurity, Robotics, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical & Computer Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Industrial & Systems Engineering, Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering, Materials Science
university_and_program_options.admission_requirements_summary: Bachelor's or Master's degree in engineering/CS with first-class grades, top research publications, and strong letters of recommendation.
university_and_program_options.easiest_hardest_institutions_guidance: College of Computing and Aerospace Engineering are among the most competitive in the United States.
university_and_program_options.strategic_program_match_advice: Research individual faculty lab pages and contact potential professors whose ongoing grants match your research background.

application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Register on the Georgia Tech graduate application portal, choose your degree program, and upload supporting files.
step_by_step_workflow: 1. Research faculty labs and active NSF/DARPA/DoD projects at Georgia Tech (September-November).
2. Create account on Georgia Tech graduate application system.
3. Select degree program (e.g. PhD in Computer Science, ECE, AE, or ME).
4. Upload Statement of Purpose, CV, transcripts, and list of publications.
5. Nominate 3 academic referees who submit online reference letters.
6. Pay application fee before deadline (typically mid-December).
7. Departmental admissions committee reviews applications and matches candidates with funded faculty labs.
8. Receive admission and financial assistantship offer (February-March).
10. Receive I-20 and apply for US F-1 visa.
application_process_roadmap.university_vs_scholarship_routing: Integrated single application: all admitted doctoral students are automatically evaluated for GRA/GTA assistantships.
application_process_roadmap.recommendation_letters_submission_method: Submitted online by 3 referees through Georgia Tech confidential portal.
application_process_roadmap.personal_statement_prompts: Statement of Purpose describing technical background, research accomplishments, publications, and specific Georgia Tech research labs of interest.
application_process_roadmap.cv_format_requirements: Academic CV detailing publications, presentations, GPA, and software/engineering competencies.
application_process_roadmap.interview_format_details: Supervisors conduct 30-45 minute technical video interviews.
application_process_roadmap.standardized_tests: GRE General test is optional or not required for most engineering and computing schools.
application_process_roadmap.attestation_requirements: Unofficial transcripts uploaded during application; official attested transcripts required upon admission.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Scanned copy of valid international passport
Transcripts for all completed post-secondary degrees with grading scales
Confidential reference letters from research mentors and professors
Technical essay detailing research trajectory, publications, and specific Georgia Tech faculty alignment
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Highlight specific Georgia Tech lab projects
Sent to Georgia Tech institutional code 5248

important_dates_timeline.annual_cycle_notes: Single annual intake; December 15 deadline observed for all funding consideration.

selection_process_and_weights.personal_statement_weight: 10% (Technical clarity and alignment with Georgia Tech faculty)
selection_process_and_weights.selection_panel_composition: School Graduate Admissions Committees and individual research faculty members.
selection_process_and_weights.evaluation_methodology: Faculty supervisor review and nomination -> School graduate committee ranking -> Formal admission and assistantship issuance.

competitiveness_profile.total_annual_applicants: ~5,000 international applicants across engineering and computing schools
competitiveness_profile.total_scholarships_awarded: ~400 to 500 fully funded PhD offers annually
competitiveness_profile.typical_academic_and_research_profile: Graduates from NUST, GIKI, FAST, UET Lahore, and LUMS with high class percentiles, international publications, and proven software/hardware laboratory skills.
competitiveness_profile.common_backgrounds_of_winners: Strong Pakistani representation in Electrical & Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and Computer Science at Georgia Tech.
competitiveness_profile.high_representation_countries: United States, China, India, South Korea, Iran, Pakistan, Turkey, Canada.

red_flags_and_warnings.application_fee_warning: Application fee of $105 is paid solely through Georgia Tech portal. Assistantships require no extra fee.
red_flags_and_warnings.agent_and_intermediary_warnings: Georgia Tech does not employ recruitment agencies or consultants.
itemized_hidden_out_of_pocket_costs: US F-1 Visa application fee and SEVIS I-901 fee (USD $535 / ~PKR 150,000)
Airfare Pakistan to Atlanta Hartsfield-Jackson (~PKR 250,000 to 350,000)
Mandatory student fees not covered by waiver (~USD $800 to $1,000/semester)
debunked_myths_and_misconceptions: MYTH: Master's students get automatic full funding. (Truth: Full assistantships with complete tuition waivers are primarily reserved for PhD candidates).
MYTH: You cannot apply directly with a Bachelor's degree. (Truth: Top Bachelor's graduates are routinely admitted directly to Georgia Tech PhD programs).
official_vs_unofficial_discrepancies: Unofficial websites claim student fees are fully waived; students pay roughly $800–$1,000/semester in mandatory campus fees.

scholarship_obligations_and_terms.minimum_gpa_maintenance: Must maintain a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 out of 4.00 and make satisfactory research progress.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.attendance_requirements: Full-time physical research residence at Georgia Tech Atlanta campus.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.academic_progress_monitoring: Annual doctoral progress review with supervisory committee; passing qualifying exams within 2 years.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.work_restrictions_during_study: Assistantship service requires 20 hours per week of research or teaching; external work strictly limited.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.home_country_return_obligation: None; graduates qualify for 3-year US STEM OPT extension and permanent residency pathways.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.repayment_clawback_conditions: Assistantship is discontinued if GPA falls below 3.00 or if the student fails departmental qualifying exams.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.rules_for_changing_major: Requires approval from both graduate programs.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.extension_policy: Funding is renewed annually throughout the doctoral degree subject to lab research grant availability.
